final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is materially better than the earlier overbroad certification theory: it now concedes that monitoring and documentation do not cure the policy issue and that the named-segment question remains unresolved. But that narrower position is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. On the available evidence, the affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, the policy treats such cases as material, and the record still lacks evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. That leaves certification presently unsupported on the admissible record, even though aggregate readiness evidence is favorable.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named-segment limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the unresolved gap.
The policy text treats weaknesses affecting a contractual customer segment or named launch use case as material, and the affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form.
Legal review remains open, so the materiality/disclosure predicate is unresolved at decision time.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public monitoring/model-card guidance do not satisfy the release-policy condition for an unresolved material limitation.
